question_text: Find the value of ¹⁰C₅ + 2·¹⁰C₄ + ¹⁰C₃.

mark_split.label: Apply Pascal once more and evaluate

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the value of 10 C 5 plus twice 10 C 4 plus 10 C 3.
insider_note: Split 2·¹⁰C₄ into two copies and pair each with the neighbour whose lower number differs by one — the sum collapses to ¹¹C₅ + ¹¹C₄ = ¹²C₅. Evaluating the three terms numerically reaches the same 792 in three times the working.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Split 2·¹⁰C₄ and pair the terms
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write 2·¹⁰C₄ as ¹⁰C₄ + ¹⁰C₄ and group (¹⁰C₅ + ¹⁰C₄) + (¹⁰C₄ + ¹⁰C₃); each bracket is a Pascal pair.

recall.must_convey: That the middle term is split into two 10 C 4 terms and paired, each pair collapsing by Pascal to 11 C 5 and 11 C 4.
accept: split two ten C four into ten C four plus ten C four and pair them, ten C five with ten C four is eleven C five and ten C four with ten C three is eleven C four
group into two Pascal pairs giving eleven C five plus eleven C four
the expression becomes eleven C five plus eleven C four
two ten C four ni split chesi pairs cheste eleven C five plus eleven C four

steps.why: The coefficient 2 is what makes the pairing possible: ¹⁰C₄ is the partner of both its neighbours, so the three terms become two Pascal pairs. This is the pattern (1 + x)² applied to Pascal.
common_mistakes: Evaluating each of the three terms numerically (252 + 420 + 120 = 792) — correct but longer and not the method being tested.
Pairing ¹⁰C₅ with ¹⁰C₃, whose lower numbers are two apart.

steps.label: Apply Pascal once more and evaluate

recall.must_convey: That 11 C 5 plus 11 C 4 is 12 C 5 by Pascal, which evaluates to 792.
accept: eleven C five plus eleven C four is twelve C five which is seven hundred ninety two
twelve C five equals seven hundred and ninety two
Pascal tho twelve C five, seven ninety two
twelve into eleven into ten into nine into eight by one twenty

steps.why: The two results of step 1 are themselves a Pascal pair, so the whole expression is one combination, ¹²C₅. The question asks for a value, so it must be evaluated.
common_mistakes: Stopping at ¹²C₅ without a number.
Computing 12·11·10·9·8 = 95040 and dividing by 24 instead of 120.
